sections.title: Rational-Belief Standard and Cumulative Case
sections.rationale: This opening section establishes the governing distinction between rationality and truth, then pairs it with the cumulative theistic conclusion that the debate subsequently tests across several evidential domains.

moveAssignments.rationale: This move supplies the debate-wide standard of rational belief against which the later constructive arguments and exchanges are organized.
This move states the cumulative theistic conclusion that integrates the later lines concerning rationality, design, and morality.

sections.title: Evil, Salvation Confusion, and Divine Character
sections.rationale: This section groups the early challenges from apparently gratuitous suffering and disputed salvation conditions with the later theistic concessions, defenses, and creator-versus-classical-God synthesis.

moveAssignments.rationale: This is a load-bearing statement of the apparent-gratuitous-evil challenge to the specified all-powerful and all-loving God.
The evil-God comparison provides a major structural test of whether possible reconciliations adequately address the suffering challenge.
This move introduces the distinct salvation-confusion burden concerning grave consequences and disagreement about necessary beliefs.
This move develops the salvation-confusion line through the disputed and inaccessible salvation-hoop formulation.
The concession identifies suffering as the principal counterevidence before the section turns to the proposed theistic responses.
This reply connects the experience of suffering to a normative account of how the world ought to be.
This reply introduces afterlife restoration as a major component of the proposed accounting for earthly suffering.
This move consolidates the section's named theodicies and the claim that God participates in and responds to suffering.
This synthesis connects the suffering dispute to whether any inferred creator can be identified with the specified classical God.

sections.title: Evolution and the Reliability of Reason
sections.rationale: This section contains the evolutionary reliability case for theism and the ensuing exchange over naturalism, truth-tracking, adaptive cognition, and whether theism faces an analogous reliability problem.

moveAssignments.rationale: This move states the principal constructive contrast between unguided minds and reason grounded in an intelligent creator.
This move supplies the detailed evolutionary argument that natural selection targets advantageous behavior rather than truth.
This reply separates atheism from naturalism and raises the adaptive-cost challenge to systematically false cognition.
This move develops the evolutionary account of broadly accurate but imperfect cognition as a major opposing step.
This reply restates the theistic truth-directed account and contrasts it with cognition directed toward evolutionary success.
This move closes the exchange by arguing that inaccessible divine reasoning creates an analogous trust problem for theism.

sections.title: Fine-Tuning and Natural Accounts of Design
sections.rationale: This section pairs the fine-tuning argument from narrow life-permitting physical conditions with the later evolutionary account offered as an alternative explanation for apparent biological design.

moveAssignments.rationale: This move is the section's load-bearing constructive statement of fine-tuning as evidence for intelligent design.
This move supplies the section's principal naturalistic alternative by locating apparent biological design within evolutionary explanation.

sections.title: Objective Morality and the Ground of Goodness
sections.rationale: This section follows the moral argument from objective obligations through evolutionary explanation, the divine-command dilemma, the historical biblical reply, divine-nature grounding, and the final restatement.

moveAssignments.rationale: This move states the load-bearing moral argument that objective moral law requires grounding and is explained by God.
This reply offers social evolution as an alternative account of moral intuitions, care, sacrifice, and religious resonance.
This move introduces the central dilemma between morality independent of God and morality defined by divine command.
This reply connects the moral standards used in criticism to the historical influence of biblical human dignity.
This move gives the principal divine-nature response by grounding objective goodness in God as the personal creator.
This closing reply argues that identifying God with goodness restates rather than removes the underlying dilemma.

bridgeMappings.rationale: The retained evidence spans the opening rational-belief standard and the later evil, salvation, and divine-identity material that carries the motion-level pro route.
The mapping preserves the cumulative-case reference in the opening frame and the concentrated evidence concerning evil, epistemic confusion, salvation, and identification of the proposed God.

All retained evidence for the suffering subsidiary is concentrated in the section containing apparent gratuitous evil, the evil-God comparison, concessions, theodicies, restoration, and divine identity.

The two retained salvation-confusion moves are assigned together because they state the disagreement over salvation requirements and develop the inaccessible-hoop consequence within one topical section.
The retained evidence is distributed across the three relevant domains: evolved cognition and reason, natural explanations of apparent design, and evolutionary or independent accounts of morality.
The cumulative conclusion is retained in the opening frame, while its three constructive evidential components remain assigned to the reason, design, and morality sections.
This mapping retains the cumulative conclusion, each positive evidential line, and the responses to suffering across their topical sections, preserving the complete central route structure.
All retained evidence concerning evolved minds, truth-tracking, intelligent creation, and the reciprocal reliability challenge is assigned to the dedicated reason section.

The fine-tuning constructive and natural-design alternative are grouped in the design section, while the later creator-identification synthesis remains in the divine-character section where it occurs topically.

The complete retained morality exchange is assigned to one section, covering objective moral law, evolutionary explanation, the divine-command dilemma, biblical influence, and divine-nature grounding.
